sources.entry: Python: _Building a Coding Agent From Scratch_

summary.one_liner: An open-source, self-paced course in which you build "decode," a Python coding agent from scratch, with a headless harness around a Pydantic AI tool-calling loop.
keywords: learn to build an ai agent
summary.what_it_does: The repository is a course plus a codebase for a coding agent called decode. The core is a Pydantic AI ReAct-style loop that alternates between model requests and tool calls, with about nine tools covering file I/O, bash, web, todo, skills, LSP and asking the user. The README describes a headless core with two front ends: an interactive terminal UI built on prompt_toolkit and Rich, and remote runs on Modal serverless functions triggered by CLI, webhook, or cron. Other described layers include a permission system (allow/ask/deny), a sandbox seam (host, Docker, or Modal), context compaction around 80% of the window, memory files (AGENTS.md / MEMORY.md), an agents catalog (build, plan, code reviewer, explore), and session recording and replay through Kitaru. Evals run on Opik with a benchmark and a regression suite. The layout is organized as one Python package under src/decode with matching tests, docs/adr, and evals directories.
use_cases: learn how coding agents work internally
build a custom agent for another domain
run open-weight models through a coding agent
sandbox agent shell commands in Docker or Modal
run agents headlessly on a schedule or via webhook
benchmark and regression-test an LLM agent
record and replay agent runs for debugging
how_to_run: git clone the repository and cd into building-a-coding-agent-from-scratch-course
cp .env.example .env and set an LLM API key
Type /demo- in the TUI to pick a demo skill
Follow running_the_code/01_install_and_usage.md, then the later guides in order
notable: Teaches harness engineering: the agent loop is about 20 lines, and the surrounding harness (tools, permissions, sandbox, memory, compaction, replay, evals) is the course
One headless core exposed through an interactive TUI and through Modal serverless remote runs
Hand-rolled stdio LSP client and a permission layer, built without agent frameworks beyond Pydantic AI
Eight written lessons and six videos accompany the code, with a guide per stage under running_the_code/
Lessons cover recording runs in Kitaru and turning failed traces into a regression suite
caveats: Several steps depend on third-party accounts and services: Modal credits, Opik, Kitaru, and an LLM API key; the README says the default Gemini tier has limited requests
Full course takes roughly 4-8 hours, and running all code takes 6-8 hours
Remote and Modal-based features require Modal setup; the README links separate guides for each step
